title: Fix it: export orders to the csv the finance team imports
basics: With `output application/csv`, an Array of flat Objects is written as CSV: the keys of the first Object become the header row and each Object becomes a line. The columns come out in the order the keys appear in each Object.
prompt:
The script in the editor is **almost** right. It passes on the sample and fails on a case you cannot see.

The original task was:

Finance imports a CSV with exactly these columns, in this order: `id,customer,total`.

Orders arrive as JSON with the customer nested, `{ id, customer: { name }, total }`. `total` must be written with exactly two decimals, so `9.5` becomes `9.50`. An order whose customer is not known yet has no `customer` object; leave that cell empty.

Find what is wrong and fix it. You can press Run to see what it currently does.
starter:
%dw 2.0
output application/csv
---
payload map ($ update { case c at .customer -> c.name })
hints: Run it on the sample first. If the sample looks right, the bug only shows on data the sample does not contain.
Ask what kind of input would break this — an empty list, a missing field, a value ordered differently.
copies each order and only flattens the customer, so the columns follow the input's key order
solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/csv
---
payload map { id: $.id, customer: $.customer.name, total: $.total as String {format: "0.00"} }

mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/csv
---
payload map ($ update { case c at .customer -> c.name })

explanation.approach: CSV has no nesting and no types, so each row is built as a flat Object with the columns in the order finance expects, and the total is formatted as text. The column order comes from the Object you build, which is why copying the input shape breaks when an upstream system reorders its keys.

snippets.label: A null value is an empty cell
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/csv
---
[{ id: 4, customer: null, total: "5.75" }]

snippets.label: Columns follow the Object
snippets.note: The header is built from the keys as written.
